newsitem.title: USA: Gumbel says new show won't be sensationalistic.
newsitem.headline: Gumbel says new show won't be sensationalistic.

text.p: Bryant Gumbel, who joined CBS's news team earlier this year, said Thursday his new prime-time television magazine program would not be like many of the tabloid television shows currently broadcast.

"I promise you ... we are not going to be bottom-feeders," Gumbel told reporters at CBS's semiannual tour for television writers. Gumbel was referring to the proliferation of sensational tabloid television shows airing in the U.S.
CBS and Gumbel have been spare with details on the content and format of the show, which will air this fall on Wednesdays at 2100 Eastern time.
The show will be called "Public Eye with Bryant Gumbel."
Gumbel said the broadcast would emphasize live studio elements focussing on "story telling" and investigative pieces.

Five correspondents were named as regular contributors to the show, including Bernard Goldberg and Peter Van Sant, both CBS news veterans; Alison Stewart, a former reporter for Viacom Inc's MTV; Maggie Cooper, a reporter from WCBS-TV in New York; and Derek McGinty, a Washington radio talk-show host.
Gumbel said he had no plans to anchor the CBS evening news in the future or broadcast sports events, and he dismissed speculation he might run for political office.
His appearance followed a controversial appearance by Rep. Susan Molinari, who plans to leave politics to become a CBS news anchor next month.

Gumbel said his production company will have two television programs "up and running" for syndication next year. As part of his contract with the network, CBS will fund several programs for television syndication, to be produced by Gumbel's production company.
He declined to give any details on the new shows.
Gumbel joined CBS earlier this year after spending 25 years with General Electric Co's NBC, including a long stint as co-anchor of The Today Show.
CBS is a unit of Westinghouse Electric Corp.
